status: Hypothetical iris assumptions; only the colorimetry tables are standard data

colorimetry.colour_space: CIE 1976 L*a*b*; white is a perfect reflector under the same sampled tables

notes: Absorbance values are single-pass over the stroma at 550 nm for the combined melanins.
Eumelanin and pheomelanin spectra are power laws with declared exponents; they are illustrative shapes, not measured spectra.
A steeper pheomelanin exponent means less red absorption than eumelanin; it is the assumption that lets pheomelanin shift hue.
Backscatter is bounded Rayleigh-like (fraction at 550 nm times (550/lambda)^exponent, capped at 1).
The translucent_red_return modes stand in for a reddish return through a pigment-poor, translucent iris. Five plateau strengths are swept because the strength is assumed, not measured.
A scenario is classified only if its luminance Y is at least the stated fraction of the reference's, so very dark pigment-saturated cases are not counted as orange or purple.
Colour uses the CIE tables in cie-tables/, sampled at the model wavelengths. CIELAB hue angle does not change when a spectrum is uniformly dimmed, so brightness and hue are judged separately.
D65 is a reference daylight, not a viewing condition. Real appearance also depends on lighting, adaptation, surroundings and camera processing.
Windows are hue-angle ranges centred on reference spectra chosen for this exploration; they are not definitions of the words orange or purple.
